extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and grant applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIH framework that reorganizes the prior five regulatory review criteria into three factors for applications with due dates January 25, 2025 or later; two factors receive numerical scores (1-9) and one is assessed for adequacy. Provides reviewer guidance on what to evaluate under each factor and which additional criteria inform overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 1: Importance of the Research (Significance and Innovation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring: 1-9. Combines Significance and Innovation elements; reviewers assess how the proposed work addresses critical gaps or creates conceptual advances and whether it employs novel concepts or applies existing methods in new ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance: Evaluate how the proposed work addresses critical gaps or creates conceptual advances; consider "the importance of the proposed research in the context of current scientific challenges and opportunities" and whether rigorous scientific background justifies the study. Innovation: Determine if the project employs novel concepts or applies existing methods in new ways. Note that critical research may not require technical innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 2: Rigor and Feasibility (Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring: 1-9. Examines Approach, including both rigor and feasibility components, and includes consideration of clinical trial timelines and inclusion adequacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigor elements: Evaluate potential for "unbiased, reproducible, robust data," experimental design quality, sample size justification, analysis plans, and biological variable considerations (sex, age). For human/animal studies, assess intervention quality, outcome variables, generalizability, and population diversity appropriateness. Feasibility elements: Determine if approaches are "sound and achievable" with contingency planning. For human studies, evaluate recruitment/retention capacity and enrollment likelihood across demographic categories. Also consider clinical trial timelines and adequacy of plans for inclusion across relevant groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3: Expertise and Resources (Investigators and Environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation: Sufficient or Gaps Identified (No Numerical Score). Assesses the investigators' qualifications and the institutional environment/resources for executing the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators: Assess whether researchers demonstrate appropriate "background, training, and expertise" for their career stage. For multiple-PI applications, evaluate leadership coordination plans. Environment: Confirm institutional resources "are appropriate to ensure the successful execution of the proposed work." Report whether expertise and resources are sufficient or if gaps are identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Criteria — items considered in overall impact (no separate scores)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of criteria that inform overall impact but are not scored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered in overall impact but without separate scores: Human subjects protections (when applicable); Vertebrate animal welfare; Biohazard evaluation; Resubmission/renewal/revision appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects protections
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, human subjects protections are evaluated and factored into overall impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human subjects protections specifically evaluate five areas: risk levels, protective measures, benefits, importance of the knowledge to be gained, and safety monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animal welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the welfare considerations for vertebrate animal research when applicable, included in overall impact considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazard evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of biohazard risks and mitigation when applicable, factored into overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission/renewal/revision appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of whether a resubmission, renewal, or revision is appropriate and justified, considered in overall impact.
